drafted_from: tool:write-message-models-for-every-app's row in tools/write-message-models-for-every-app/tool-rows.json, do-work/write-message-models.mjs, read-data/sample-models.json and test/write-message-models.test.mjs; the answers were observed by running the script on a copy of the sample models file
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check whether the Swift and TypeScript message models under my app folder are behind my models.json, and if they are, write them." It runs write-message-models.mjs on your computer, first with --check, then with --write.
no_lists_because: It keeps no account list: its models are rows in one JSON file on the person's computer, and it writes source files from that file.
instructions: 1. Write your models file in the shape of read-data/sample-models.json: models (each {name, doc, fields: [{name, type, optional?, doc?, mutable?}]}, type String, Int, Bool, a model name or a one-element list) and targets (mac, ios, typescript: the file each is written to under the root, and for Swift the protocols, the Swift type name each model takes and which models are Identifiable).

2. Say where it is and which folder holds the app sources. The AI reads the row with @workshop-tools tools:list {tool: "tool:write-message-models-for-every-app"}, then from the root of the Workshop checkout runs node tools/write-message-models-for-every-app/do-work/write-message-models.mjs --models models.json --root <app folder> --check.

3. Read the result. --check prints nothing and exits 0 when every file is current; it exits 1 and says on standard error "Behind <models file>: <files>" when any is behind. Run it again with --write (the default) to bring them up to date: it prints "Wrote <files>", or "Up to date." when nothing was behind.
4. Change a model by editing a row in the models file and running --write again, never by editing a generated file: each carries a header that says so.

worked_examples.title: Write the three files for the sample notice models, then check
worked_examples.ask: Write my message models for the apps and the web from models.json.
worked_examples.given: Run for real with a copy of tools/write-message-models-for-every-app/read-data/sample-models.json saved as models.json, and an empty folder root: node tools/write-message-models-for-every-app/do-work/write-message-models.mjs --models models.json --root root --check, then the same with --write, then --check again.
worked_examples.hands_back: The first --check exits 1 and prints on standard error: "Behind models.json: macos/Shared/DeviceBridgeModels.swift, ios/Notices/DeviceBridgeModels.swift, src/device-bridge-models.d.ts. Run: node write-message-models.mjs --models models.json --write". --write prints "Wrote macos/Shared/DeviceBridgeModels.swift, ios/Notices/DeviceBridgeModels.swift, src/device-bridge-models.d.ts". The last --check prints nothing and exits 0. root/macos/Shared/DeviceBridgeModels.swift starts "// generated from models.json by write-message-models.mjs; change the rows there and run the script, never this file" and holds struct NoticeActionInput, struct NoticeAction: Codable, Hashable, Identifiable and struct Notice: Codable, Hashable, Identifiable with let seq: Int and var read: Bool?; the iPhone file holds only the two models its target names, as TrillionNoticeActionInput and TrillionNoticeAction.

worked_examples.title: A new field on a model makes two files fall behind
worked_examples.ask: I added a pinned field to Notice; are the models current?
worked_examples.given: From test/write-message-models.test.mjs ('a changed row makes --check fail'), run for real: after the files above were written, the Notice model in models.json gets one more field {name: pinned, type: Bool, optional: true}, then --check.
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 1 and on standard error: "Behind models.json: macos/Shared/DeviceBridgeModels.swift, src/device-bridge-models.d.ts. Run: node write-message-models.mjs --models models.json --write". The iPhone file is not listed: its target does not name Notice.
